statement: How many integers greater than $100$ and less than $400$ have exactly three positive divisors?

choices.misconception: I thought the cube of a prime has exactly three divisors because the exponent is $3$, and the only prime cubes in the range are $125$ and $343$.
I thought the square of any odd number has exactly three divisors, so I counted $11^2, 13^2, 15^2, 17^2, 19^2$, but $225 = 15^2$ has more.
I knew the number had to be a perfect square, so I counted every square from $11^2 = 121$ to $19^2 = 361$, even squares of numbers that are not prime.
I counted every perfect square from $11^2$ up to $20^2 = 400$, forgetting that $400$ is not less than $400$ and that most squares have more than three divisors.

hints: Divisors usually come in pairs. When can a number have an odd number of them?
A number with exactly three divisors must be a perfect square, $1$, $p$ and $p^2$, where $p$ is a prime.
You need primes $p$ with $100 < p^2 < 400$, that is, primes from $11$ to $19$.

solutions.reliable: Divisors pair up as $d$ and $n \div d$, so an odd number of divisors means $n$ is a perfect square. If $n = p^a q^b \cdots$, it has $(a+1)(b+1)\cdots$ divisors, and this equals $3$ only when $n = p^2$ for a prime $p$; its divisors are $1, p, p^2$. We need $100 < p^2 < 400$, so $10 < p < 20$, giving $p = 11, 13, 17, 19$. The numbers are $121, 169, 289, 361$: there are $4$.
